permutation_invisible_under_constant_pla.claim: apply_permutation(constant_array, pi) == constant_array for ANY pi
permutation_invisible_under_constant_pla.implication: A chosen all-zero (or any constant-byte) plaintext bypasses observing the permutation stage entirely -- diffusion then operates directly on the constant input. This does not leak S/pi/a/b to an attacker (the ciphertext bytes still pass through the full forward+backward diffusion chain, which remains unknown), but it IS a structural degenerate case worth recording: confusion (permutation) contributes nothing against constant-plaintext inputs; all observed nonlinearity for such inputs comes solely from the diffusion stage's S-box.

single_bit_propagation_note: If propagation fraction is markedly position-dependent (e.g. flips near the END changing fewer bytes than flips near the BEGINNING), that would indicate asymmetric diffusion strength -- expected in principle, since forward diffusion chains left-to-right from the flip point and backward diffusion then chains right-to-left over ALL of u, so a flip anywhere should in theory reach the full ciphertext. See diffusion_analysis.py for the isolated, non-combined measurement of each pass.

two_time_pad_style_xor_check.description: Classical two-time-pad attacks on C=P XOR K (K reused) rely on C1 XOR C2 == P1 XOR P2 -- i.e. the keystream K cancels exactly under XOR. This construction has no such additive-XOR keystream step at the top level (addition is mod 256 through an S-box, not XOR with a fixed keystream), so this check establishes whether that specific classical structure is present.
two_time_pad_style_xor_check.conclusion: chi2 close to the theoretical mean under uniformity indicates the XOR of the two ciphertexts shows no obvious two-time-pad-style structure recoverable by simple XOR-cancellation. This does NOT prove general nonce-reuse safety (see nonce_analysis.py's equation-counting discussion and the final report's Track B section) -- it only rules out the SPECIFIC classical stream-cipher XOR-cancellation attack, which does not apply to this construction's algebraic form.
